summary: Intermittent p99 spikes and 5xxs on dedicated reservation during overlap with long-sequence batch jobs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (LexicoHealth) reports intermittent high p99 latency and spike in 5xx (504/503) for inference requests served from their dedicated reservation in us-west during overnight windows. The behavior started 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC and recurred multiple times overnight.

Impact:
- Several production endpoints returned elevated p99 (1.2s -> 7s) and 5xx rate climbed to 8% for short intervals (~2-6 minutes).
- Business impact: LexicoHealth ingests inference results into user workflows; timeouts cause retries that fail end-user flows. They flagged this as production-severity for multiple services.

Environment:
- Dedicated reservation: lexicon-prod-resv-usw (dedicated GPU pool).
- Region: us-west.
- Models in use: starcoder-3b for long-code-completion paths; redwood-v2-medium for short chat.
- Autoscaler config: min_replicas: 0, max_replicas: 8, scale_target_cpu: 70%.

Steps to reproduce / observed pattern:
1) Schedule synthetic load that mixes long-sequence batch jobs (offline-embeddings/long-seq-batch) with online short chat traffic at similar time.
2) When long-sequence jobs enter the pool and overlap with online traffic, p99 for online requests jumps and 5xxs appear.
3) When long-seq jobs finish or are evicted, latency returns to baseline.

Logs / quick artifacts:
- Customer-provided timestamped traces: s3://lexicohealth-logs/2026-03-12/inference-traces/trace_20260312_0210.json (redacted link).
- Support trace snippet: "request_id=abc123 host=gpu-node-04 p99_ms=6400 backend_error=timed_out"
- Monitoring charts: heatmap of per-pod GPU context switches and memcopy stalls attached in investigation section.

Customer message (initial):
"We're seeing intermittent timeouts overnight. We didn't change workloads this week; this started when an internal large-embedding batch ran. Please advise; this is blocking our nightly ingest."
investigation:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC: Support triage; confirmed elevated p99 and 5xx spikes in LexicoHealth reservation.
- 2026-03-12 04:10 UTC: SRE noticed correlation with scheduled "offline-embedding-batch" (another tenant) running in same physical dedicated cluster due to pool labeling overlap.
- 2026-03-12 04:40 UTC: Captured NVML metrics and scheduler events; observed repeated GPU context-switch counts and spikes in PCIe memcopy time on affected nodes.

Hypotheses considered:
1) Noisy neighbor running long-sequence jobs causing KV cache thrashing and memory copies, increasing tail latency for co-located online inference.
2) Autoscaler mis-sized (min_replicas=0) allowed cluster to scale down overnight; when batch job arrived, scaling up lag + pod scheduling placed long-seq pods on same hosts as online pods causing contention.
3) Thermal/clock throttling on several GPUs due to sustained peak from the batch job leading to transient slowdowns.

Findings:
- GPU utilization profile shows high memcpy_util and lower compute_util during spike windows -> indicates memory-bound long sequences causing heavy host-device transfers.
- Node metrics: GPU power draw elevated, and dmesg contains a few nvlink timeouts on gpu-node-04 (nonfatal).
- Autoscaler logs: scale up triggered but new pods came up 45-90s after first performance degradation (scaling lag). With min_replicas=0 there was insufficient warm capacity.
- Scheduler placement: long-seq batch pods had no anti-affinity rules, so they colocated with LexicoHealth online pods.

Correlated artifacts:
- Slack thread: #support-lexicohealth (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C02ABCDEF/p1647043200000)
- Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood/prod/lexicohealth/panels/latency-2026-03-12
- Node metric snapshot (support): https://storage.redwood.com/tmp/node-snapshot-20260312.png

Interim mitigation attempted:
- At 2026-03-12 06:10 UTC we temporarily increased lexicon-prod-resv-usw min_replicas to 2 for LexicoHealth service and pushed pod anti-affinity for their online pods to prefer distinct nodes. Immediate p99 reduced but not fully back to baseline until long-seq batch finished.
comments: 2026-03-12 03:15 - Ava Morgan (Support): Acknowledged issue with customer and requested traces / sample request IDs.
2026-03-12 04:25 - Diego Ruiz (SRE): Observed matching spike windows in node GPU memcpy time. Opening investigation; correlating with off-hour heavy batch job. See slack thread #support-lexicohealth.
2026-03-12 05:00 - LexicoHealth (Customer): We can schedule batch jobs outside of our online windows but need a long-term fix — this impacts SLAs.

2026-03-12 06:20 - Diego Ruiz (SRE): Applied temporary config change: min_replicas=2 for lexicon-prod-resv-usw and added anti-affinity preference. Monitoring results; p99 reduced ~60% in first 10 minutes.

2026-03-13 09:40 - Maya Chen (Product): Noted that default autoscaler templates set min_replicas=0 for cost-saving; flagging as product follow-up to add dedicated-pool recommended defaults for enterprise reservations.

2026-03-14 11:12 - Quentin Li (Platform): Linked a potential scheduler patch PR to allow long-seq job isolation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4182 — needs QA and rollout planning.
next_steps:
Short-term: enforce min_replicas>=1 for dedicated reservations for customers with production SLAs and apply anti-affinity heuristics for online latency-sensitive pods.
Medium-term: introduce scheduling class for long-sequence batch jobs and a placement policy to prevent colocation with latency-sensitive online pods; add autoscaler warm pool / burst capacity options for dedicated.
Action Items:
- (SRE) Roll forward autoscaler minimum change to lexicon-prod-resv-usw across region (diego) — in progress.
- (Platform) QA PR #4182 for scheduler isolation and plan phased rollout (quentin).
- (Support/Product) Update onboarding checklist and recommended reservation templates for enterprise (maya/ava).
notes: This ticket is intentionally technical and operational; runbook reference added. Recommend follow-up postmortem if customer requests formal RCA.
